[list]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Defeat all[/b] – the classic.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Hold out[/b] – survive a set number of rounds, then the Echoes withdraw.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Break through[/b] – get a unit to the ladder to escape.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Bounty[/b] – slay the marked champion; its underlings lose heart.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Defend the Crystal[/b] – protect a destructible Echo crystal for several rounds (lose it = floor lost). You can heal it to keep it alive.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Rescue the captive Echo[/b] – its guards attack it; clear the floor before it dies to earn a [b]Recruit Ticket[/b] for a brand-new unit.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Loot the vaults[/b] – open the visible treasure chests (some are guarded).[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Cut off the runner[/b] – kill the fleeing loot Echo before it escapes.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Flawless[/b] – clear the floor without losing a unit.[/size][/color][/*]
[*][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]Purge the nests[/b] – destroy the nests before they bleed reinforcements.[/size][/color][/*]
[/list][color=#ff0000][size=3][b][u]Surprise attacks[/u][/b][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=3][b]:[/b] hidden dormant enemies that spring when you get close, and telegraphed mid-battle reinforcement waves.
[b]Rewards:[/b] rescuing an Echo grants a Recruit Ticket; treasure chests and the runner drop loot sacks (gear, materials, gold, crystals, consumables, rare seals); completing special objectives pays bonus Echo Crystals.
Everything is configurable in GMCM [/size][/color]

[u][color=#00ff00][size=4][b]Instead of replacing the vanilla mines, this mod adds an alternative mine mode[/b][/size][/color][color=#ffffff][size=4]. [/size][/color][/u]

[u][color=#ffffff][size=4]Starting from Year 1, Day 7, a small story event introduces strange sounds coming from below. After that, whenever you interact with the mine elevator, you can choose whether you want to enter the normal mines or the new Echo Mines. [/size][/color][/u]

[color=#ffffff][size=4][b]The Echo Mines are designed as an additional activity, not a replacement. You can try them early, ignore them for a while, or return later when you feel ready [/b][/size][/color]

[i][u][color=#ffff00][size=4][b]What ist Stardew Tactics?[/b][/size][/color][/u][/i]

[color=#ff7700][size=4][i]The Echo Mines transform mining into a turn-based tactical strategy game inspired by:[/i][/size][/color]

[color=#ff00ff][size=4][i]- Fire Emblem
- Final Fantasy Tactics
- Octopath Traveler
- Darkest Dungeon[/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ff7700][size=4][i]
You command a squad of units on tactical maps, move them turn by turn, attack enemies, collect resources, unlock jobs, build skill loadouts and uncover the mystery of the Echoes.
At the beginning, you receive six starting units: the Stardew Valley Bachelorettes. They are sent into the mines to investigate strange voices and unnatural disturbances coming from below.
Deep inside, they encounter the Echoes: mysterious fallen heroines connected to the Adventurer’s Guild. Who they are, why they are appearing, and what will happen if they escape is still unknown.
But one thing is clear:
They must be stopped.[/i][/size][/color]

[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]FEATURES: [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]

[color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]IMPORTANT: [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]This MOD has a lot of features.... ! Please read it all to ensure your up to the challange!!!!! [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]

[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Tactical Turn-Based Combat[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Combat is played on tactical maps with grid-based movement and turn-based decision making.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Positioning matters.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Unit roles matter.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Enemy weaknesses matter.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Team composition matters.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Each battle becomes a mix of movement, resource gathering, class strategy and enemy control. [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]

[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]The deeper you go, the more dangerous and complex the encounters become.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Break System[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]The Echo Mines include a Break System inspired by Octopath Traveler.
Enemies and units can have specific weaknesses, such as being vulnerable to certain weapon types or combat categories. If a target is hit enough times with attacks it is weak against, its Break protection is reduced.
For example, if an Echo is [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]weak[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b] to Blade attacks, hitting it twice with blade-based attacks from different units — or triggering a double attack — can [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]break it.
A broken unit becomes stunned and vulnerable, creating powerful tactical openings.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
However, this system works both ways.
Your own units can also be broken if you ignore enemy strengths and weaknesses. You must pay attention to enemy attack types, resistances and Break conditions, or your squad can quickly lose control of the fight.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Echo Affinities and Enemy Bonds[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]The Echoes are not just isolated enemies.
Some Echoes can have affinities with each other, allowing them to become stronger when fighting together. Similar to your own bonding system, enemy bonds can create dangerous combinations and make certain groups much harder to deal with.
This means you cannot only look at one enemy at a time. You also need to consider how Echoes support each other, how close they are, and which targets should be broken or defeated first.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Additive Mine Loot System[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]The Echo Mines include their own additive loot system. Completing battles rewards you with resources based on how deep you are in the mine.
Early areas may reward basic materials such as copper.
Deeper floors can reward iron, gold and rarer resources.
The better and faster you perform, the better your rewards can be.
Enemies can also drop additional loot in several rarities:
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#783f04][size=5][i][u][b]Common[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#00ff00][size=5][i][u][b]Uncommon[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#1e84cc][size=5][i][u][b]Rare[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#9900ff][size=5][i][u][b]Epic[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#e69138][size=5][i][u][b]Legendary[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Some drops are normal resources, while others are special upgrade items used for the tactical progression system itself.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Tactical Mining[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Mining is part of the strategy.
Units do not mine manually. [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#00ffff][size=5][i][u][b]Instead, when a unit moves through stones, ore or obstacles, they automatically break them and collect the loot.
This creates an extra tactical layer[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]: movement is not only about reaching enemies, but also about collecting resources efficiently.
Broken rocks can even damage nearby enemies if they shatter close enough, turning movement routes into offensive opportunities.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Job Class System[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Every unit begins as a Novice.
From there, units can unlock and train many different job classes. These include basic classes such as sword fighters, clerics, brawlers and other early roles, as well as advanced classes such as:
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#00ffff][size=5][i][u][b]- Monk
- Samurai
- Brawler
- Stormbringer
- Yandere
- Priestess
- Summoner[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
and many more.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Each class earns its own Job Points, inspired by Final Fantasy Tactics. Job Points can be spent to unlock skills inside the currently used class.
However, learned skills are not automatically active forever. You build a loadout.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]

[color=#ff7700][size=5][i][u][b]A unit can equip a main class and a subclass, allowing powerful combinations[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]. For example, you could create a Samurai with Priestess as a subclass, giving that unit access to both sword techniques and healing abilities.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Random Level-Ups and Growth Rates[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Units grow through a random level-up system.
When a unit levels up, stat increases are not fixed. Instead, each class and unit type has different growth tendencies.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
A physical fighter such as a Samurai is more likely to gain strength.
A Priestess or Mage is more likely to gain willpower or magical stats.
A Brawler may develop differently from a ranged attacker or support unit.
This gives every unit a slightly different identity over time. Even two units using similar jobs can grow in different ways depending on their class path, luck and role.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Mastery Requirements[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Class progression also uses a mastery system inspired by Fire Emblem: Three Houses.
Advanced jobs require specific combat mastery ranks. For example, becoming a Samurai may require a very high Blade rank.
Mastery categories include:
Blade
Strike[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Healing
Magic
Ranged[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
This means your units grow based on how you actually use them. A character who fights with swords will naturally progress toward blade-focused classes, while a magic user can develop toward magical roles.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Bonding Between Units[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Units can build bonds by fighting together.
As relationships grow, they unlock additional combat effects and team-based mechanics. One example is the chance for a double attack, where a bonded ally may join in during combat.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
This system rewards building consistent teams, keeping allies close, and developing your favorite combinations over time.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
Bonding also interacts with combat strategy, because double attacks can help trigger Breaks faster.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Light and Danger System[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Inspired by Darkest Dungeon, the Echo Mines become more dangerous as the battle continues.
Each round, the light slowly fades. As darkness increases, your units may suffer negative effects while the Echoes grow stronger.
To survive longer battles, you may find torches that restore light and reduce the pressure.
The deeper you go, the more important light management becomes.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Progression and Savepoints[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]The Echo Mines start relatively easy, but become much harder in the deeper floors.
Like the vanilla mine, the Echo Mines include regular savepoint-style progression every five floors:
5, 10, 15, 20, and so on.
This allows you to secure progress and push deeper over time instead of starting from the beginning every run.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Echo Crystals, Shop and Recruitment[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]After each run, you earn Echo Crystals based on your performance.
Echo Crystals can be spent in a special shop to buy useful items such as:
Healing potions
Weapons
Upgrade items
Recruitment items
One of the most important systems is the Recruiter.
With recruitment items, you can create new units for your squad. The recruitment system is inspired by classic RPG character creation. You can choose a portrait, select a sprite, and then roll the unit’s stats.
You receive a limited number of free rolls. After that, additional rolls cost currency. This creates a risk-and-reward system: you may get a strong rare or epic unit early, or you can keep rolling and risk ending up with weaker stats.
With enough Echo Crystals, you can continue searching for the perfect recruit.
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[line]
[heading][color=#ff0000][size=5][i][u][b]Dynamic Combat Presentation[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][/heading]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]Combat is designed to feel dramatic and stylish.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
When attacking major Echo enemies, the game can switch into a special combat vignette, inspired by Fire Emblem. [/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]

[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]The camera focuses on the attacker and target, making important attacks feel more cinematic.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
[color=#ffff00][size=5][i][u][b]
The combat system includes:
[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color][color=#ff7700][size=5][i][u][b]- Double attacks
- Critical hits
- Portrait cut-ins
- Breaks and stuns
- Dynamic attack presentation
- Special combat visuals against Echoes
- Critical hits can trigger portrait cut-ins, making battles feel more intense and rewarding.[/b][/u][/i][/size][/color]
